clue.text: Lift humble criminal a small amount

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A thief lifts a modest item from someone humble, a petty crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun describing who lifts things, but it is the anagram signal working on LIFT HUMBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: As much as fits in the tiny sewing cap, the word is a stock measure for a very small quantity.

indicators.note: during says the bishop's letter sits within the period of the word for play

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop gets mugged while watching a play.
explanation.walkthrough: A Toby jug is a British drinking mug shaped like a seated man in a tricorn hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby is a kind of jug or tankard, a mug moulded as a jolly figure.

clue.text: Force Time to support popular short film

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up, or supports, the pieces above it

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a flick is informal for a film

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to make time to back a popular short film.
explanation.definitionFit: To force a penalty or blow on someone is to impose it; a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: playfully, standing next to one's own double or twin self

explanation.surface: Someone is distraught, perhaps from meeting a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frantic with emotion; read literally it means positioned next to your own self, as with a double.

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
an acting manager is a deputy standing in for someone

explanation.surface: A one-time stand-in is described as hard to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding, hard-to-satisfy task or person is a synonym for difficult.

indicators.note: segment of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a painful, narrow section of a broken bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the ulna, a forearm bone, so it stands for that bone loosely.

indicators.note: framing says the copper-and-succeeded pair encloses the son like a picture frame

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman curses after managing to frame a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, chemical symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse or utter oaths is a colloquial synonym for swearing.

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
a chain is a group of shops under one owner

explanation.surface: An advertisement for free entry to swanky newly opened shops.
explanation.definitionFit: To release from fetters or bonds is to set loose, a verb synonym.

indicators.note: contracted means the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
an A-list person is a top celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous artist signs a contract with a county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like signing a deal but means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of the Dalí or Magritte movement is a kind of artist; an example.

parts.note: to buff is to polish

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Instructions for polishing one side of something first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' could be the nationality; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiasts or devotees of a hobby are called this, an informal synonym for fans.

parts.note: suggests someone collected between shows, but means a broadcaster whose voice is picked up by listeners in the gaps between programmes

explanation.surface: Someone collected from a venue in the interval between shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuity presenter's voice is heard, or picked up, between broadcast programmes.

clue.text: Camping in club with a student is not part of the plan

indicators.note: in says the camping phrase goes inside the word for club

parts.note: a union is an association or club, as in a students' union
camping means staying in a tent
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Going camping with a student in the club was never planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the camping phrase inside the word for club; L for student is the British learner-driver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done by accident rather than design was never part of the plan.

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are arranged oddly, in a new order

explanation.surface: When tea and dinner are served is oddly unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a link; the fodder is TEA plus DINNERTIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Not fixed or definitely known, so vague and unsettled; a synonym.

clue.text: Possible to excuse lover if bag is repaired

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A partner can be forgiven if a damaged bag is mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be pardoned means an offence can be excused; a synonym.

clue.text: Make a bigger leap away from home?

definitions.meaning: to out-jump someone, beating them by bounding further

explanation.surface: Someone jumps further to get away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as out plus bound it means outjump; as one word it describes travel heading outward from base.

clue.text: Stuck in Fiat on a lane without key

indicators.note: stuck in says the answer is lodged inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a Fiat on a country lane.
explanation.definitionFit: Music with no tonal centre is written without a key; a technical synonym.

indicators.note: short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a manifesto is a party's statement of policy

explanation.surface: A politician unveils a brief statement of policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To show plainly or display is a verb synonym for revealing something.

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder or mistake

explanation.surface: A pundit asks whether the boss has blundered.
explanation.walkthrough: A gaffer is British slang for a boss, especially a football manager.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for a boss or foreman, often a football club's manager.

clue.text: Satisfying affair, one pound to get in

indicators.note: to get in says the next pieces enter the word for affair

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A rewarding romance that costs only a pound to join.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal that fills you up is satisfying; an adjective synonym.

definitions.meaning: starts or sets in motion, as a campaign or a rocket
motorboats carried by ships or used for ferrying

explanation.surface: Someone embarks in small craft.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means starts or sends off; the noun names motor boats, a plural of a kind of vessel.

clue.text: According to Spooner, street rental is mad

indicators.note: Spooner was an Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a way is a road or street, as in Broadway
hire is the renting of something

explanation.surface: The cost of renting on this street is crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone wrong or out of control, an idiom for erratic, crazy behaviour.

clue.text: Brute and villain played on unknown weakness

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: Y is one of the letters used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Actors cast as brute and villain play on an unknown flaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' signals the anagram; 'and' and 'on' are only links, and Y is the algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open to attack or harm is a form of weakness; a near synonym.

clue.text: A spirit boxing ace shows once more

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the spirit is placed around the ace

parts.note: gin is a spirit
A is the abbreviation for an ace in cards

explanation.surface: A boxer who drinks spirits shows his ace form again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated a second time; an adverb synonym meaning anew.

parts.note: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: Women call off their strike, or the industrial action is scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb but is a noun, a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bit or iota, as in not a bit of difference; a synonym for scrap.

clue.text: Place to keep papers in short trial

parts.note: brief means short
a court case is a trial

explanation.surface: A lawyer's papers kept during a brief court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat case with a handle for carrying documents is a place to keep papers.

clue.text: Broadcast denial that's heard at Aintree?

indicators.note: broadcast says the word is spoken out, so we go by its sound

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a denial

explanation.surface: A denial aired on the radio during the Grand National.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National, so horses are heard there.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a horse would be heard at a racecourse; a definition by example.

definitions.meaning: to inch or creep forward gradually
the outer limit or border of something

explanation.surface: Creeping slowly toward a point of danger.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to inch along; the noun means a rim or outermost limit.

clue.text: Energy lacking in terribly sentimental episode

indicators.note: terribly says the remaining letters are badly jumbled
lacking says one letter must be taken away from the following word

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soap episode is terribly sentimental and lacks energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes one E from SENTIMENTAL, and 'terribly' shuffles the ten letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: One part of a serial story issued in sequence is a synonym for an episode.
